claims.evidence: This is inferred from the structural arrangement in the open state.

claims.claim: The conformational change moves F80 and F84 away from the center of the pore and involves rotation of the neck helix along its helical axis (~15 ° clockwise viewed from the extracellular side).
claims.source: The conformational change moves F80 and F84 away from the center of the pore and involves rotation of the neck helix along its helical axis (~15 ° clockwise viewed from the extracellular side) and outward displacement of the neck helix that is more pronounced on its N-terminal end (~2.5 Å at F80).
claims.evidence: This is measured from structural comparison.

claims.claim: The conformational change involves outward displacement of the neck helix that is more pronounced on its N-terminal end (~2.5 Å at F80).
claims.source: The conformational change moves F80 and F84 away from the center of the pore and involves rotation of the neck helix along its helical axis (~15 ° clockwise viewed from the extracellular side) and outward displacement of the neck helix that is more pronounced on its N-terminal end (~2.5 Å at F80).
claims.evidence: This is measured from structural comparison.

claims.claim: The opening transition includes a slight expansion of the entire transmembrane region of the channel (~1 Å increase in radius).
claims.source: The opening transition includes a slight expansion of the entire transmembrane region of the channel (~1 Å increase in radius), and a coordinated set of side chain rotamer changes (Figure 2A,B, Figure 2—video 1).
claims.evidence: This is measured from structural comparison.

claims.claim: Both F80 and F84 move from the most commonly observed rotamer for phenylalanine in the closed conformation to the second most commonly-observed rotamer in the open conformation.
claims.source: Both F80 and F84 move from the most commonly observed rotamer for phenylalanine (observed 44% of the time in the PDB) in the closed conformation to the second most commonly-observed rotamer (observed 33% of the time) in the open conformation (Lovell et al., 2000).
claims.evidence: This is supported by rotamer analysis and the cited reference.

claims.claim: F80 and F84 rotate away from the axis of the pore by 80° and 105°, respectively.
claims.source: By these conformational changes, F80 and F84 rotate away from the axis of the pore (by 80o and 105o, respectively, Figure 2, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is measured from structural comparison.

claims.claim: Accompanying side chain rotamer changes occur among neighboring residues (Y236, F282, F283, and W287) to allow for the movements of F80 and F84.
claims.source: Accompanying side chain rotamer changes that occur among neighboring residues (Y236, F282, F283, and W287) allow for the movements of F80 and F84 (Figure 2A,B, Figure 2—video 1).
claims.evidence: This is observed from structural comparison.

claims.claim: When the channel opens, the first α-helical turn of the neck helix unravels such that I76 packs with F247, F276, L279 and F283 in the open conformation and has shifted by approximately 10 Å.
claims.source: When the channel opens, the first α-helical turn of the neck helix unravels such that I76 packs with F247, F276, L279 and F283 in the open conformation and has shifted by approximately 10 Å (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is measured from structural comparison.

claims.claim: The unraveling of the first α-helical turn of the neck helix is facilitated by P77, which is perfectly conserved among BEST channels.
claims.source: The unraveling is facilitated by P77, which is perfectly conserved among BEST channels and is part of the neck helix in its closed conformation, but marks its N-terminal end in the open conformation (Figure 2C,D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by structural comparison and sequence conservation.

claims.claim: P77 is part of the neck helix in its closed conformation, but marks its N-terminal end in the open conformation.
claims.source: The unraveling is facilitated by P77, which is perfectly conserved among BEST channels and is part of the neck helix in its closed conformation, but marks its N-terminal end in the open conformation (Figure 2C,D).
claims.evidence: This is observed from structural comparison.

claims.claim: The repositioning within the neck exposes the hydrophilic residues S79 and G83 on the neck helix to the pore in its open conformation.
claims.source: The repositioning within the neck also exposes the hydrophilic residues S79 and G83 on the neck helix, which had been secluded behind the F80 and F84, to the pore in its open conformation (Figure 2A,B, Figure 2—video 1).
claims.evidence: This is observed from structural comparison.

claims.claim: S79 and G83 had been secluded behind F80 and F84 in the closed conformation.
claims.source: The repositioning within the neck also exposes the hydrophilic residues S79 and G83 on the neck helix, which had been secluded behind the F80 and F84, to the pore in its open conformation (Figure 2A,B, Figure 2—video 1).
claims.evidence: This is observed from structural comparison.

claims.claim: Through a concertina of coordinated conformational changes in and around the neck helix, amino acids that formed the hydrophobic barrier that prevented ion permeation have dispersed and reveal a wide aqueous vestibule.
claims.source: Thus, through a concertina of coordinated conformational changes in and around the neck helix, amino acids that formed the hydrophobic barrier that prevented ion permeation have dispersed and reveal a wide aqueous vestibule, the diameter of which would be large enough to allow permeation of hydrated halide ions and larger molecules as well.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the structural changes observed.

claims.claim: The diameter of the open neck would be large enough to allow permeation of hydrated halide ions and larger molecules as well.
claims.source: Thus, through a concertina of coordinated conformational changes in and around the neck helix, amino acids that formed the hydrophobic barrier that prevented ion permeation have dispersed and reveal a wide aqueous vestibule, the diameter of which would be large enough to allow permeation of hydrated halide ions and larger molecules as well.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the measured diameter of the open neck.

claims.claim: The cryo-EM structure of BEST1345 in the absence of Ca2+ is indistinguishable from a cryo-EM structure of Ca2+-free BEST1405 at 3.6 Å resolution.
claims.source: The structure is determined to 3.0 Å resolution and is indistinguishable from a cryo-EM structure of Ca2+-free BEST1405 at 3.6 Å resolution.
claims.evidence: This is supported by structural comparison.

claims.claim: The overall structure of the Ca2+-free channel is very similar to the inactivated and Ca2+-bound closed conformations with the only notable differences near the Ca2+ clasp.
claims.source: The overall structure of the channel is very similar to the inactivated and Ca2+-bound closed conformations with the only notable differences near the Ca2+ clasp.
claims.evidence: This is supported by structural comparison.

claims.claim: W287 is perfectly conserved among metazoan bestrophin channels and even conserved in the prokaryotic KpBEST channel.
claims.source: W287 is perfectly conserved among metazoan bestrophin channels and even conserved in the prokaryotic KpBEST channel (Yang et al., 2014) (Figure 4A); this sequence conservation would be consistent with an important role in channel gating.
claims.evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment and the cited reference.

claims.claim: W287 is positioned approximately at the midpoint between the Ca2+ clasp and the neck.
claims.source: W287 is also positioned approximately at the midpoint between the Ca2+ clasp and the neck (Figure 2A,B).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the structure.

claims.claim: W287 adopts one side chain rotamer to pack with F80 and F84 in the open conformation and a different side chain rotamer in the closed conformation that buttresses the space between adjacent neck helices.
claims.source: W287 adopts one side chain rotamer to pack with F80 and F84 in the open conformation and a different side chain rotamer in the closed conformation that buttresses the space between adjacent neck helices (Figure 2A,B, Figure 4E,F).
claims.evidence: This is observed from structural comparison.

claims.claim: The W287F mutation produces channels with dramatically altered gating.
claims.source: We find that the W287F mutation (BEST1345 W287F) produces channels with dramatically altered gating.
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings.

claims.claim: BEST1345 W287F retained normal Cl- versus K+ selectivity.
claims.source: Whilst BEST1345 W287F retained normal Cl- versus K+ selectivity (Figure 4B), the W287F mutation constitutively activates the channel, making it nearly insensitive to the presence or absence of Ca2+.
claims.evidence: This is supported by reversal potential measurements.

claims.claim: The W287F mutation constitutively activates the channel, making it nearly insensitive to the presence or absence of Ca2+.
claims.source: Whilst BEST1345 W287F retained normal Cl- versus K+ selectivity (Figure 4B), the W287F mutation constitutively activates the channel, making it nearly insensitive to the presence or absence of Ca2+.
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings showing current maintained in the absence of Ca2+.

claims.claim: Approximately 80% of the Cl- current level through BEST1345 W287F is maintained when Ca2+ was chelated with EGTA, whereas currents through wild type BEST1 drop to zero.
claims.source: Approximately, 80% of the Cl- current level through BEST1345 W287F is maintained when Ca2+ was chelated with EGTA, whereas currents through wild type BEST1 drop to zero (Figure 4B,C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by electrophysiological recordings.

claims.claim: Cryo-EM structures of BEST1345 W287F in the presence and absence of Ca2+ were determined at 2.7 Å and 3.0 Å resolutions, respectively.
claims.source: To understand the molecular basis of this behavior, we determined cryo-EM structures of BEST1345 W287F in the presence and absence of Ca2+ at 2.7 Å and 3.0 Å resolutions, respectively (Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2).
claims.evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claims.claim: In the presence of Ca2+, BEST1345 W287F adopts an open conformation that is essentially indistinguishable from the open conformation observed for BEST1345.
claims.source: In the presence of Ca2+, BEST1345 W287F adopts an open conformation that is essentially indistinguishable from the open conformation observed for BEST1345 (Figure 4—figure supplement 3, Cα RMSD = 0.2 Å).
claims.evidence: This is supported by structural comparison showing RMSD of 0.2 Å.

claims.claim: 3D classification of the BEST1345 W287F dataset did not reveal a closed conformation, which indicates that essentially all of the particles are in an open conformation.
claims.source: Unlike BEST1345, 3D classification of the BEST1345 W287F dataset did not reveal a closed conformation, which indicates that essentially all of the particles are in an open conformation and that the open state is preferential for this mutant.
claims.evidence: This is supported by 3D classification analysis.

claims.claim: The open state is preferential for the BEST1345 W287F mutant.
claims.source: Unlike BEST1345, 3D classification of the BEST1345 W287F dataset did not reveal a closed conformation, which indicates that essentially all of the particles are in an open conformation and that the open state is preferential for this mutant.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the absence of closed conformations in 3D classification.

claims.claim: In the absence of Ca2+, and in spite of missing density for Ca2+ and a disordered Ca2+-clasp region, the neck of BEST1345 W287F also adopts an open conformation.
claims.source: Remarkably, in the absence of Ca2+, and in spite of missing density for Ca2+ and a disordered Ca2+-clasp region, the neck also adopts an open conformation (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by the cryo-EM structure.

claims.claim: The W287F mutation decouples Ca2+ binding from the conformational changes in the neck that are observed for the wild type channel.
claims.source: Thus, in accord with the electrophysiological recordings, the W287F mutation decouples Ca2+ binding from the conformational changes in the neck that are observed for the wild type channel.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the structural and electrophysiological data.

claims.claim: Modeling of the W287F mutation on a closed conformation of the channel introduces a void behind the neck.
claims.source: Modeling of the W287F mutation on a closed conformation of the channel introduces a void behind the neck (Figure 4—figure supplement 3E), which we hypothesize energetically disfavors the closed conformation.
claims.evidence: This is based on molecular modeling.

claims.claim: The void introduced by the W287F mutation energetically disfavors the closed conformation.
claims.source: Modeling of the W287F mutation on a closed conformation of the channel introduces a void behind the neck (Figure 4—figure supplement 3E), which we hypothesize energetically disfavors the closed conformation.
claims.evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the modeling results.

claims.claim: The open pore of BEST1 comprises a 90 Å-long water-filled vestibule and a short constriction at the cytosolic aperture.
claims.source: The structures reveal that the open pore of BEST1 comprises a 90 Å-long water-filled vestibule and a short constriction at the cytosolic aperture (Figure 1D).
claims.evidence: This is measured from the structures.

claims.claim: The aperture is located approximately 55 Å from the neck.
claims.source: The aperture, which is located approximately 55 Å from the neck, is only ~3 Å long (measured where the pore diameter is <4 Å); its walls are formed solely by the V205 side chains of the five subunits (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This is measured from the structures.

claims.claim: The aperture is only ~3 Å long (measured where the pore diameter is <4 Å).
claims.source: The aperture, which is located approximately 55 Å from the neck, is only ~3 Å long (measured where the pore diameter is <4 Å); its walls are formed solely by the V205 side chains of the five subunits (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This is measured from the structures.

claims.claim: The walls of the aperture are formed solely by the V205 side chains of the five subunits.
claims.source: The aperture, which is located approximately 55 Å from the neck, is only ~3 Å long (measured where the pore diameter is <4 Å); its walls are formed solely by the V205 side chains of the five subunits (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This is observed from the structures.

claims.claim: Retinitis pigmentosa can be caused by mutation of the corresponding I205 residue of human BEST1 to threonine.
claims.source: Retinitis pigmentosa can be caused by mutation of the corresponding I205 residue of human BEST1 to threonine (Davidson et al., 2009).
claims.evidence: This is supported by the cited reference.

claims.claim: The aperture adopts the same conformation in all of the structures of BEST1 determined to date, regardless of whether the neck is open or closed or whether or not Ca2+ is bound.
claims.source: The aperture adopts the same conformation in all of the structures of BEST1 determined to date, regardless of whether the neck is open or closed or whether or not Ca2+ is bound (Figure 1C,D, Figure 3, Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
claims.evidence: This is supported by structural comparison.

claims.claim: The aperture does not function as either the activation or the inactivation gate.
claims.source: We have concluded previously from electrophysiological studies that the aperture does not function as either the activation or the inactivation gate (Vaisey and Long, 2018; Vaisey et al., 2016), and the structural data support this conclusion.
claims.evidence: This is supported by cited electrophysiological studies and structural data.

claims.claim: The V205A mutation of chicken BEST1 has no effect on Ca2+-dependent activation or inactivation.
claims.source: Accordingly, the V205A mutation of chicken BEST1, which would be expected to widen the aperture markedly, has no effect on Ca2+-dependent activation or inactivation (Vaisey and Long, 2018; Vaisey et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is supported by the cited references.

claims.claim: Mutations of V205 have dramatic effects on ion permeability.
claims.source: Mutations of V205 do, however, have dramatic effects on ion permeability (Vaisey et al., 2016) (Figure 5C,D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This is supported by permeability measurements.

claims.claim: Both human and chicken BEST1 exhibit a lyotropic relative permeability sequence in which permeable anions that are more easily dehydrated than Cl-, such as Br-, I- and SCN-, are more permeable than Cl-.
claims.source: Both human and chicken BEST1 exhibit a lyotropic relative permeability sequence in which permeable anions that are more easily dehydrated than Cl-, such as Br-, I- and SCN-, are more permeable than Cl- (Vaisey et al., 2016; Qu and Hartzell, 2000; Hartzell et al., 2005; Hille, 2001) (Figure 5C, PX/PCl ~ 2.7 when X = Br, ~5.1 when X = I and ~14.4 when X = SCN).
claims.evidence: This is supported by permeability measurements and cited references.

claims.claim: The lyotropic permeability sequence is an indication that at least partial dehydration occurs for ions as they permeate through the channel.
claims.source: The lyotropic permeability sequence is an indication that at least partial dehydration occurs for ions as they permeate through the channel.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the permeability data and is established knowledge.

claims.claim: The aperture is the only constriction where dehydration would occur in the open channel.
claims.source: Given the structural context of the open channel, the aperture is the only constriction where dehydration would occur (Figure 1D,E); the dimensions of the aperture are too narrow for a hydrated ion to pass and therefore the aperture would necessitate that anions shed at least some water molecules as they pass through it.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the pore dimensions.

claims.claim: The dimensions of the aperture are too narrow for a hydrated ion to pass.
claims.source: Given the structural context of the open channel, the aperture is the only constriction where dehydration would occur (Figure 1D,E); the dimensions of the aperture are too narrow for a hydrated ion to pass and therefore the aperture would necessitate that anions shed at least some water molecules as they pass through it.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the measured dimensions of the aperture.

claims.claim: The aperture necessitates that anions shed at least some water molecules as they pass through it.
claims.source: Given the structural context of the open channel, the aperture is the only constriction where dehydration would occur (Figure 1D,E); the dimensions of the aperture are too narrow for a hydrated ion to pass and therefore the aperture would necessitate that anions shed at least some water molecules as they pass through it.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the dimensions of the aperture.

claims.claim: The aperture is responsible for the lyotropic permeability sequence.
claims.source: The structures support the conclusion that the aperture is responsible for the lyotropic permeability sequence (Vaisey et al., 2016).
claims.evidence: This is supported by structural data and the cited reference.

claims.claim: Mutation of V205 to a smaller residue (e.g. glycine, alanine, or serine) abolishes the lyotropic sequence among Cl-, Br-, I- and SCN-.
claims.source: Consistently, we find that mutation of V205 to a smaller residue (e.g. glycine, alanine, or serine) abolishes the lyotropic sequence among Cl-, Br-, I- and SCN- (Figure 5C), which suggests that the aperture is made sufficiently wide by these mutations to allow these ions to pass without dehydration.
claims.evidence: This is supported by permeability measurements.

claims.claim: The aperture is made sufficiently wide by mutations to glycine, alanine, or serine to allow Cl-, Br-, I- and SCN- to pass without dehydration.
claims.source: Consistently, we find that mutation of V205 to a smaller residue (e.g. glycine, alanine, or serine) abolishes the lyotropic sequence among Cl-, Br-, I- and SCN- (Figure 5C), which suggests that the aperture is made sufficiently wide by these mutations to allow these ions to pass without dehydration.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the permeability data.

claims.claim: Mutation of V205 to isoleucine makes the lyotropic permeability differences between Cl-, Br-, I- and SCN- more dramatic.
claims.source: In contrast to the effects of small amino acids, mutation of V205 to isoleucine, a bulkier hydrophobic amino acid that would presumably reduce the diameter of the aperture, makes the lyotropic permeability differences between Cl-, Br-, I- and SCN- more dramatic (Figure 5C).
claims.evidence: This is supported by permeability measurements.

claims.claim: Ions shed more water molecules when passing through the V205I aperture than through the wild type one.
claims.source: These effects suggest that ions would shed more water molecules when passing through the V205I aperture than through the wild type one.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the permeability data.

claims.claim: The aperture controls permeability among halide anions by causing ion dehydration.
claims.source: Thus, the aperture controls permeability among halide anions by causing ion dehydration, and it thereby engenders the characteristic lyotropic permeability sequence of BEST1.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the structural and permeability data.

claims.claim: The aperture engenders the characteristic lyotropic permeability sequence of BEST1.
claims.source: Thus, the aperture controls permeability among halide anions by causing ion dehydration, and it thereby engenders the characteristic lyotropic permeability sequence of BEST1.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the structural and permeability data.

claims.claim: The relative permeability of the channel to acetate, propionate and butyrate increases when V205 is substituted with the smaller alanine or glycine residues.
claims.source: We found that the relative permeability of the channel to acetate, propionate and butyrate increases when V205 is substituted with the smaller alanine or glycine residues (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by permeability measurements.

claims.claim: When the aperture is made wider by mutation, larger organic anions are more permeable.
claims.source: Thus, when the aperture is made wider by mutation, larger organic anions are more permeable.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the permeability data.

claims.claim: The aperture functions in the wild type channel as a size-selective filter.
claims.source: These data support the previous inference (Vaisey et al., 2016) that the aperture functions in the wild type channel as a size-selective filter.
claims.evidence: This is supported by permeability data and the cited reference.

claims.claim: The aperture would tend to prevent the permeation of large cellular constituents such as proteins or nucleic acids but would allow smaller solutes such as Cl- ions to pass.
claims.source: The aperture would tend to prevent the permeation of large cellular constituents such as proteins or nucleic acids but would allow smaller solutes such as Cl- ions to pass.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the size-selective properties of the aperture.

claims.claim: The aperture is not perfectly discriminatory for the smallest solutes, as indicated by the measureable permeability of the wild type channel to acetate.
claims.source: However, the data indicate that the aperture is not perfectly discriminatory for the smallest solutes, as indicated by the measureable permeability of the wild type channel to acetate (Figure 5D).
claims.evidence: This is supported by permeability measurements.

claims.claim: The amino acid sequence at and around amino acid 205 varies among human BEST1-4 channels and among bestrophin channels in general.
claims.source: Notably, the amino acid sequence at and around amino acid 205 varies among human BEST1-4 channels and among bestrophin channels in general (Figure 5B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by sequence alignment.

claims.claim: Sequence variability at the aperture may endow BEST1-4 channels with distinct permeabilities related to their specific physiological functions and their particular biological locations.
claims.source: This sequence variability at the aperture may endow BEST1-4 channels with distinct permeabilities related to their specific physiological functions and their particular biological locations.
claims.evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the sequence variability and permeability data.

claims.claim: The structures represent the major gating transitions in the metazoan bestrophin channel.
claims.source: The structures presented herein represent the major gating transitions in the metazoan bestrophin channel.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the multiple conformational states captured.

claims.claim: When unoccupied by Ca2+, the Ca2+ clasps are disordered, the neck is closed, and ions are prevented from permeating through the channel by the neck.
claims.source: When unoccupied by Ca2+, the Ca2+ clasps are disordered, the neck is closed, and ions are prevented from permeating through the channel by the neck.
claims.evidence: This is supported by the Ca2+-free structure.

claims.claim: When Ca2+ ions bind, the Ca2+ clasps become ordered and the open and closed conformations of the channel have free energies that are similar enough that the neck can sample both conformations.
claims.source: When Ca2+ ions bind, the Ca2+ clasps become ordered and the open and closed conformations of the channel have free energies that are similar enough that the neck can sample both conformations.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the observation of both open and closed conformations in the Ca2+-bound dataset.

claims.claim: The open conformation of the neck is dramatically wider than the closed conformation.
claims.source: The open conformation of the neck is dramatically wider than the closed conformation and opening (activation) exposes small hydrophilic amino acids to the pore where large hydrophobic ones had been.
claims.evidence: This is supported by pore dimension analysis.

claims.claim: Opening (activation) exposes small hydrophilic amino acids to the pore where large hydrophobic ones had been.
claims.source: The open conformation of the neck is dramatically wider than the closed conformation and opening (activation) exposes small hydrophilic amino acids to the pore where large hydrophobic ones had been.
claims.evidence: This is observed from structural comparison.

claims.claim: The wide neck explains why the neck has essentially no influence on ion selectivity.
claims.source: The wide neck explains why the neck has essentially no influence on ion selectivity (Vaisey et al., 2016), in spite of speculation that it might be involved in ion selectivity from the initial X-ray structure of BEST1 (Kane Dickson et al., 2014) and the structure of KpBest (Yang et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the wide dimensions of the open neck and cited references.

claims.claim: The channel inactivates at higher concentrations of Ca2+ through a mechanism that involves the binding of the C-terminal inactivation peptide to its receptor.
claims.source: The channel inactivates at higher concentrations of Ca2+ through a mechanism that involves the binding of the C-terminal inactivation peptide to its receptor.
claims.evidence: This is supported by structural data and cited references.

claims.claim: The receptor for the inactivation peptide is on the cytosolic surface of the channel.
claims.source: The receptor is on the cytosolic surface of the channel and the binding of the inactivation peptide to it allosterically controls the conformation of the neck from a distance.
claims.evidence: This is observed from the structures.

claims.claim: The binding of the inactivation peptide to its receptor allosterically controls the conformation of the neck from a distance.
claims.source: The receptor is on the cytosolic surface of the channel and the binding of the inactivation peptide to it allosterically controls the conformation of the neck from a distance.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the structural data showing the inactivation peptide bound and the neck closed.

claims.claim: The inactivated conformation of the neck is indistinguishable from the deactivated (Ca2+-free) one.
claims.source: The inactivated conformation of the neck is indistinguishable from the deactivated (Ca2+-free) one.
claims.evidence: This is supported by structural comparison.

claims.claim: Unlike voltage-dependent K+ and Na+ channels, in which ions are prevented from flowing by different mechanisms in the inactivated and deactivated states, the same closed conformation of the neck is responsible for the deactivated and inactivated states of BEST1.
claims.source: Unlike voltage-dependent K+ and Na+ channels, in which ions are prevented from flowing by different mechanisms in the inactivated and deactivated states (Hille, 2001; Armstrong and Bezanilla, 1977), the same closed conformation of the neck is responsible for the deactivated and inactivated states of BEST1.
claims.evidence: This is supported by structural comparison and cited references.

claims.claim: BEST1 does not contain separable domains.
claims.source: Unlike many ion channels that have separate self-contained domains that are responsible for controlling channel gating, such as extracellular or intracellular ligand-binding domains, or voltage sensor domains within the membrane, which can often be studied in isolation using structural or functional approaches, BEST1 does not contain separable domains.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the structural architecture.

claims.claim: The BEST1 channel comprises a single structural unit that resembles a barrel, with a portion of the barrel embedded in the membrane and a portion exposed to the cytosol.
claims.source: The BEST1 channel comprises a single structural unit that resembles a barrel, with a portion of the barrel embedded in the membrane and a portion exposed to the cytosol.
claims.evidence: This is observed from the structures.

claims.claim: The primary sequence of BEST1 does not have separate domains; rather the polypeptide portions that form the transmembrane and cytosolic regions of the channel are dispersed throughout the primary sequence.
claims.source: Additionally, the primary sequence of BEST1 does not have separate domains; rather the polypeptide portions that form the transmembrane and cytosolic regions of the channel are dispersed throughout the primary sequence (Kane Dickson et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This is supported by sequence analysis and the cited reference.

claims.claim: The midsection of the barrel contains the region that functions as a gate (the neck).
claims.source: The midsection of the barrel contains the region that functions as a gate (the neck) and the cytosolic surface of the barrel is decorated with sensors that influence the gate – namely the Ca2+ clasps and the inactivation peptide receptors.
claims.evidence: This is observed from the structures.

claims.claim: The cytosolic surface of the barrel is decorated with sensors that influence the gate – namely the Ca2+ clasps and the inactivation peptide receptors.
claims.source: The midsection of the barrel contains the region that functions as a gate (the neck) and the cytosolic surface of the barrel is decorated with sensors that influence the gate – namely the Ca2+ clasps and the inactivation peptide receptors.
claims.evidence: This is observed from the structures.

claims.claim: The sensors function as integral parts of the channel as a whole and could not be studied in isolation.
claims.source: These sensors, which function as integral parts of the channel as a whole and could not be studied in isolation, modulate the energetics of opening and closing of the neck through allosteric means.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the structural architecture.

claims.claim: The sensors modulate the energetics of opening and closing of the neck through allosteric means.
claims.source: These sensors, which function as integral parts of the channel as a whole and could not be studied in isolation, modulate the energetics of opening and closing of the neck through allosteric means.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the structural data and functional studies.

claims.claim: The sensors relay information received at the surface of the channel, such as the binding of Ca2+ or the inactivation peptide, through the core of the protein to the neck.
claims.source: The sensors do so by relaying information received at the surface of the channel, such as the binding of Ca2+ or the inactivation peptide, through the core of the protein to the neck.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the structural data.

claims.claim: The design of the neck appears well suited to receive subtle energetic information in that the neck comprises five helices (the S2b neck helices) that are tethered on each end by linker regions that allow the helices to toggle between two preferred orientations that form the closed and open conformations of the neck.
claims.source: The design of the neck itself appears well suited to receive this subtle energetic information in that the neck comprises five helices (the S2b neck helices) that are tethered on each end by linker regions that allow the helices to toggle between two preferred orientations that form the closed and open conformations of the neck.
claims.evidence: This is inferred from the structural features of the neck.

claims.claim: In bestrophin, cytosolic sensors on the surface of the channel control a dramatic molecular choreography within the core of the protein that underlies gating and reveals a fascinating new gating mechanism among ion channels.
claims.source: Thus, while localized twisting or domain motions that are instigated by separate sensor domains often constitute the activation mechanism of ion channels, in bestrophin cytosolic sensors on the surface of the channel control a dramatic molecular choreography within the core of the protein that underlies gating and reveals a fascinating new gating mechanism among ion channels.
claims.evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the structural data presented.

claims.claim: The electrophysiological and structural data suggest that the aperture remains essentially fixed throughout the Ca2+-dependent activation and inactivation processes.
claims.source: Our electrophysiological and structural data suggest that the aperture remains essentially fixed throughout the Ca2+-dependent activation and inactivation processes.

results.result: A 3.1 Å resolution cryo-EM structure of Ca2+-bound BEST1405 without antibody is indistinguishable from the previously published X-ray structure (RMSD 0.5 Å) and represents a Ca2+-bound inactivated state with the inactivation peptide bound.
results.evaluation: Claims C33-C34 are well-supported by structural data showing excellent agreement (RMSD 0.5 Å) between cryo-EM and X-ray structures, with clear density for bound inactivation peptides. This validates that the X-ray structure represents an inactivated state (C32) and demonstrates methodological consistency between crystallography and cryo-EM.

results.result: Cryo-EM analysis of Ca2+-bound BEST1345 reveals two distinct conformations: a closed conformation (86% of particles, 3.0 Å resolution) with a narrow neck, and an open conformation (14% of particles, 2.9 Å resolution) with a dramatically widened neck (~13 Å diameter).
results.evaluation: Claims C37-C43 are strongly supported by 3D classification showing two distinct particle populations with well-resolved structures at high resolution. The particle distribution (86% closed, 14% open) provides quantitative evidence for the energetic favorability of the closed state. The structural data clearly demonstrate the dramatic widening of the neck in the open conformation.

results.result: In the absence of Ca2+, BEST1345 adopts a closed conformation (3.0 Å resolution) with a closed neck identical to the inactivated state, disordered Ca2+ clasps, and conformational flexibility manifested as ~5° rotation between transmembrane and cytosolic regions, suggesting Ca2+ binding rigidifies the channel.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C49 are well-supported by structural data showing missing density for Ca2+ clasps, closed neck conformation, and 3D classification revealing conformational flexibility. However, C50 is speculative about the necessity of rigidification for opening. The structural observations are solid, but the mechanistic interpretation requires further validation.

results.result: Opening of the bestrophin pore involves dramatic repositioning of tethered S2b neck helices within a surrounding protein shell, widening the neck from <3.5 Å to ~13 Å through coordinated conformational changes including helix rotation (~15°), outward displacement (~2.5 Å at F80), side chain rotamer changes, and partial helix unraveling facilitated by conserved P77.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C51-C79 are comprehensively supported by detailed structural comparisons between open and closed states, with precise measurements of distances, angles, and rotamer changes. The structural data clearly demonstrate the concertina-like mechanism involving coordinated movements of I76, F80, F84, and surrounding residues. The role of P77 in facilitating helix unraveling is supported by both structural data and sequence conservation.

results.result: The neck serves as both the activation and inactivation gate in BEST1 channels, preventing ion flow when closed (in Ca2+-free, Ca2+-bound closed, and inactivated states) and permitting flow when open, with the same closed conformation responsible for both deactivated and inactivated states.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C21, C30, C58, C125-C129, C134-C135 are strongly supported by structural data showing the neck in multiple functional states, combined with cited electrophysiological studies. The structural evidence clearly demonstrates that the neck adopts the same closed conformation in Ca2+-free, Ca2+-bound closed, and inactivated states, distinguishing BEST1 from voltage-gated channels where different mechanisms underlie deactivation and inactivation.

results.result: Ca2+ binding instigates opening of the neck through allosteric coupling mediated by W287, a perfectly conserved residue positioned between the Ca2+ clasp and neck. The W287F mutation constitutively activates the channel, maintaining ~80% current in the absence of Ca2+, and locks the neck in an open conformation regardless of Ca2+ binding.
results.evaluation: Claims C6, C82-C94 are strongly supported by sequence conservation data, structural analysis showing W287 adopts different rotamers in open vs closed states, electrophysiological recordings demonstrating Ca2+-independent activity of W287F, and cryo-EM structures showing the mutant adopts an open conformation even without Ca2+. The convergence of structural, functional, and evolutionary evidence provides compelling support for W287's role in allosteric coupling.

results.result: An aperture formed by V205 side chains (~3 Å long, located ~55 Å from the neck) controls anion permeability through size-selective filtering and enforced dehydration, generating the characteristic lyotropic permeability sequence (SCN- > I- > Br- > Cl-). The aperture remains fixed during gating transitions.
results.evaluation: Claims C8, C97-C117, C147-C149 are comprehensively supported by structural data showing the aperture dimensions, structural comparison demonstrating it remains unchanged across gating states, permeability measurements showing lyotropic sequence, and mutagenesis studies where smaller residues abolish the lyotropic sequence while larger residues enhance it. The convergence of structural and functional data strongly supports the aperture's role as a size-selective filter.

results.result: The aperture functions as a size-selective filter that limits permeation of larger organic anions (acetate, propionate, butyrate), with permeability increasing when V205 is mutated to smaller residues (alanine, glycine), though the filter is not perfectly discriminatory as wild-type channels show measurable acetate permeability.
results.evaluation: Claims C118-C122, C150 are well-supported by permeability measurements showing increased permeation of organic anions with aperture-widening mutations. The data demonstrate size-selectivity while acknowledging imperfect discrimination. The functional measurements are consistent with the structural dimensions of the aperture.

results.result: Inactivation peptide binding to its receptor on the cytosolic surface allosterically controls neck conformation from a distance, inducing closing of the neck at high Ca2+ concentrations (>500 nM).
results.evaluation: Claims C7, C27, C131-C133 are supported by structural data showing the inactivation peptide bound in closed conformations, the spatial separation between the receptor and neck, and cited electrophysiological studies. The structural evidence clearly demonstrates the allosteric mechanism, though the detailed pathway of conformational coupling could be further elucidated.

results.result: Sequence variability at and around position 205 among BEST1-4 channels and bestrophin homologs may endow distinct permeation properties related to specific physiological functions, suggesting broader and more nuanced roles than currently appreciated.
results.evaluation: Claims C123-C124, C155-C156 are based on sequence alignment showing variability at the aperture region. While C123 is supported by data, C124, C155, and C156 are speculative hypotheses about functional implications. The sequence variability is documented, but the proposed functional consequences require experimental validation across different bestrophin paralogs.

results.result: The widened neck in the open conformation makes GABA permeation more structurally plausible than previously thought, though thermal motions or regulatory mechanisms affecting the aperture may be required for molecules of GABA's size to permeate at physiologically relevant rates.
results.evaluation: Claims C151-C154 are largely speculative. C151 cites a proposal about GABA permeation, and C152 correctly notes the open neck is wider than the X-ray structure, but C153-C154 are hypotheses about thermal fluctuations and regulatory mechanisms without experimental support. The structural data make GABA permeation more plausible but do not demonstrate it occurs.

results.result: BEST1 comprises a single structural unit resembling a barrel without separable domains, with the neck as the gate and cytosolic sensors (Ca2+ clasps, inactivation peptide receptors) that function as integral parts modulating neck energetics through allosteric means, revealing a novel gating mechanism distinct from channels with separate sensor domains.
results.evaluation: Claims C136-C145 are well-supported by structural analysis showing the integrated architecture, sequence analysis demonstrating dispersed transmembrane and cytosolic regions, and functional data showing allosteric coupling. The structural evidence clearly demonstrates the unique architecture and the mechanistic interpretation is consistent with the data, though some aspects of the allosteric pathways remain to be fully elucidated.

results.result: Bestrophin channels are Ca2+-activated Cl- channels that assemble as pentamers with a ~95 Å long pore containing two hydrophobic constrictions (neck and aperture). Chicken BEST1 shares 74% sequence identity with human BEST1 and possesses analogous Ca2+-activation and anion-selectivity properties.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C11, C13-C16, C18 are well-established properties supported by extensive prior work (cited references) and confirmed by the structural data presented. These represent foundational characterization of the system rather than novel findings of this study.

results.result: Mutations in BEST1 cause retinal disease, with over 200 mutations linked to eye disease. BEST1 mediates a Ca2+-activated Cl- current integral to human retinal pigment epithelial function.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C9-C10, C12 are well-established facts from prior literature (supported by cited references) that provide biological context for the study. These are not novel findings but important background information.

results.result: Bestrophin channels have no sequence or structural similarity to other ion channels. The prokaryotic KpBest shares only 14% sequence identity with human BEST1, is cation-selective, and lacks the Ca2+ clasp conserved in metazoan organisms.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C17, C19 are supported by structural comparisons and cited references. These establish the unique nature of bestrophin architecture and the differences between prokaryotic and metazoan channels, providing important context for understanding the novel gating mechanism.

results.result: Prior work established that Ca2+-activation involves Ca2+ binding to cytosolic Ca2+ clasps and conformational changes in the neck, that F80/F84 mutations don't affect selectivity, that molecular simulations suggested the X-ray neck conformation creates an energetic barrier, and that BEST1 undergoes Ca2+-stimulated inactivation involving a C-terminal peptide (aa 346-367) that can be prevented by peptide removal.
results.evaluation: Claims C20, C22-C26, C28-C29, C31, C35-C36 summarize prior work from cited references that motivated the current structural studies. These are well-established findings that provide essential context but are not novel results of this manuscript.

results.result: The Ca2+-bound closed conformation with a closed neck is consistent with single channel recordings of drosophila BEST1 showing low open probability.
results.evaluation: Claim C40 is supported by the cited reference and provides functional context for the structural observation of a Ca2+-bound closed state. This represents integration of structural and functional data rather than a novel finding.

results.result: The narrowness, length, and hydrophobicity of the closed neck create an energetic barrier to ion permeation (consistent with simulations). In the closed state, hydrophobic packing among I76, F80, F84 stabilizes the conformation, while in the open state, F80 and F84 interact with Y236 and W287. The wide open neck explains why it has no influence on ion selectivity.
results.evaluation: Claims C53, C65-C66, C130 are supported by structural analysis, cited simulation studies, and prior electrophysiological work. The structural basis for the energetic barrier and the explanation for lack of selectivity effects are well-reasoned inferences from the data.

results.result: No appreciable conformational difference is present in the cytosolic region between open and closed conformations, and the aperture retains its dimensions throughout Ca2+-dependent activation and inactivation processes.
results.evaluation: Claims C56-C57, C146 are supported by structural comparison across multiple states. This negative result is important for establishing that the neck, not the aperture, is the gate, and is consistent with prior electrophysiological studies.

results.result: Opening of the neck is reminiscent of the dilation of the iris of a camera lens.
results.evaluation: Claim C59 is a descriptive analogy based on the structural changes observed. While subjective, it is a reasonable characterization of the radial expansion mechanism and is supported by the structural data and accompanying video.

results.result: The Ca2+-free BEST1345 structure (3.0 Å) is indistinguishable from Ca2+-free BEST1405 (3.6 Å), with overall structure very similar to inactivated and Ca2+-bound closed conformations except near the Ca2+ clasp.
results.evaluation: Claims C80-C81 are supported by structural comparison and demonstrate consistency between BEST1345 and BEST1405 constructs in the Ca2+-free state. This validates the use of the truncated construct and shows the major conformational differences are localized to the Ca2+ clasp region.

results.result: Modeling of the W287F mutation on a closed conformation introduces a void behind the neck, which is hypothesized to energetically disfavor the closed conformation.
results.evaluation: Claims C95-C96 are based on molecular modeling and represent a hypothesis to explain the constitutive activation phenotype. While the modeling is reasonable and consistent with the observed phenotype, this mechanistic explanation is speculative and would benefit from additional validation such as free energy calculations or additional mutagenesis.

results.result: Retinitis pigmentosa can be caused by mutation of the corresponding I205 residue of human BEST1 to threonine.
results.evaluation: Claim C101 is supported by the cited reference and provides clinical relevance for the aperture region. This is established knowledge that contextualizes the functional importance of the aperture.
